summaries.demographer: Ellias Chand is a 66-year-old married Native man living in Havre, Montana, with his wife Mary in an owned older home (Q51, Q58, Q84, Q89). He has a high school diploma, no military service, and is retired from formal employment after a career as a woodworker, cabinetmaker, and furniture repairman (Q90, Q93, Q65). His household consists of two older adults with steady but modest retirement income, occasional craft income, and adult children and grandchildren living elsewhere (Q05, Q72-Q74). His life course is strongly place-bound, with childhood, family, work, and elder identity all anchored in Havre and the surrounding Plains tribal community (Q01, Q87, Q97).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Ellias shows cautious, stability-oriented decision-making: he chose lower income and community rootedness over higher-paying work elsewhere, revealing strong identity and social utility preferences (Q02). He is loss-averse around debt and emergencies, keeps modest savings, and treats home ownership, pantry food, garden produce, tools, and relationships as buffers against uncertainty (Q61-Q63, Q82). His spending priorities favor essentials, health, family, craft materials, and community participation over discretionary consumption (Q56-Q60). He responds better to gentle routines and social accountability than strict regimentation, as seen in walking, budgeting, and health management (Q32, Q83).
summaries.political_scientist: Ellias is a regular voter and civic participant who identifies as an Independent leaning Democratic, with priorities around tribal sovereignty, health care, public lands, schools, elder services, and rural community needs (Q23, Q24, Q95, Q96). His institutional trust is conditional: he respects good local public servants and health providers but distrusts national political promises, inflammatory media, and unequal policing (Q20, Q24, Q42). He interprets Black Lives Matter through a broader Indigenous experience of racism, policing, missing persons, land, and historical harm (Q26-Q29). His civic style is deliberative and community-based, expressed through voting, workshops, elder support, mediation, and face-to-face conversation (Q16, Q17, Q23, Q29).
summaries.psychologist: Ellias presents as compassionate, conscientious, culturally grounded, slightly disorganized, and reflective, with a self-concept built around usefulness, craft, family, and elder responsibility (Q01, Q15, Q108, Q109). He manages worry and aging-related vulnerability through meditation, journaling, walking, prayer, ceremony, music, and making things with his hands (Q38, Q43, Q45, Q50). His emotional life includes anxiety-like worry but not a formal anxiety diagnosis, and he shows adaptive coping by accepting help after his arthritis flare challenged his identity as a maker (Q31, Q44, Q45). Relationally, he is interdependent rather than isolated, drawing on Mary, friends, family, elders, and younger artists while also serving as a listener and mentor for others (Q05-Q07, Q21).
